//: The TOP of a shaft, and the drive station of a lift. It is ropeway:drivestation with the crossarm's west half and both post columns DELETED: cells [3,0..4,0] and [1..2,4,0] are the drive station's own machine leg at the drive station's own block numbers with its own driveIntakeCell, so BEPylonBase.Intake, DriveSpeedOn, DeclareLoad, OwnTheHeadCell and BEDriveHousing need no change whatever. 15 cells become 8, and 30 placed blocks become 11. There is no crossarm because a shaft does not need a portal beam across the car's path - which is the whole reason a lift can go vertical where a ropeway tower runs out of headroom at 11.3 degrees.
//shaft: Read once by BEPylonBase.ShaftRole. A STRING and not a bool because the two shaft footings are not interchangeable: the head wears the sheave, owns the drive leg, and its passage facing is the machine's only heading - the car's long axis, the counterweight's lane, the plane the wheel turns in and the frame IsSpanClear lays its corridor on. SpanMath.ShaftLinkFits is what makes that structural rather than hopeful.
//shape: The plain footing's model, exactly as drivestation and tensionstation reuse it and for the same reason: a footing is a half-block plinth buried in the landing floor, and what names a station from across the room is its machine. It is ALSO load-bearing rather than lazy - EntityRopewayCabin.DropGhostPassengers puts a relogging rider at footingY + 0.5 because 'that is the top of the footing's plinth', and every shipped footing is a 0.5 plinth. A solid deck would put them inside it and a ring would put them in the shaft.

attributes.//ropePerBlock: DOUBLE a ropeway's 0.25, in JSON and with no code at all, because the machine really does hang two full-length strands: the car's and the counterweight's. A 40-block shaft costs 20 haul rope against a 40-block ropeway span's 10. This is the one lever that is free to move if the shaft turns out to be too cheap a way to climb - see docs/POWER-AND-STORAGE.md.
attributes.//driveIntakeCell: Block number 7, the same number and the same cell drivestation.json names. BEPylonBase.Intake looks the cell up BY NUMBER out of the structure's own TransformedOffsets, so a shaft head declaring the drive station's numbering resolves ropeway:drivehousing with no C# anywhere.
attributes.//multiblockStructure: The drive station's east half, byte for byte, plus a bigger sheave. Cells [3,0,0], [3,1..3,0], [1,4,0], [2,4,0] and [3,4,0] carry the drive station's own block numbers 7, 6, 4, 4 and 5; only cell [0,4,0] differs, because a bullwheel cannot be the head sheave - bullwheelrim's rope radius is 0.663 blocks, so a 180 degree wrap separates the two strands by 1.326 and the counterweight cannot pass a car whose half-length is 2.0. OwnTheHeadCell still narrows drivehead-* to this footing's own side, so a shaft head sharing a leg with a drive station satisfies at most one of them and the shared-leg bug does not re-open.
